subproblem.title: Geometry of the graph chart G(v) = x + ιv + u(v): C² immersion, injectivity, compact preimages, S ∩ Z = G(D ∩ G⁻¹S), Borel preimages
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (ι : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid P) (u : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ), ContDiffOn ℝ 2 u (ball 0 δ₁) → (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid (n + 1)) δ₁, ∀ w : Euclid (n + 1), inner ℝ (ι w) (u v) = 0) → (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid (n + 1)) δ₁, ‖u v‖ < δ₂ / 2) → (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid (n + 1)) δ₁, x + ι v + u v ∈ N) → (∀ (v : Euclid (n + 1)) (h : Euclid P), ‖v‖ < δ₁ → ‖h‖ < δ₂ → (∀ w : Euclid (n + 1), inner ℝ (ι w) h = 0) → x + ι v + h ∈ N → h = u v) → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 (fun y => x + ι y + u y) (ball 0 δ₁) ∧ (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid (n + 1)) δ₁, ∀ a : Euclid (n + 1), fderiv ℝ (fun y => x + ι y + u y) v a = ι a + fderiv ℝ u v a) ∧ (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid (n + 1)) δ₁, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun y => x + ι y + u y) v)) ∧ InjOn (fun y => x + ι y + u y) (ball 0 δ₁) ∧ IsOpen {w : Euclid P | ‖ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x)‖ < δ₁ ∧ ‖w - x - ι (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x))‖ < δ₂} ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ {w : Euclid P | ‖ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x)‖ < δ₁ ∧ ‖w - x - ι (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x))‖ < δ₂} → IsCompact (ball 0 δ₁ ∩ (fun y => x + ι y + u y) ⁻¹' K)) ∧ (∀ S : Set (Euclid P), S ⊆ N → S ∩ {w : Euclid P | ‖ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x)‖ < δ₁ ∧ ‖w - x - ι (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap (w - x))‖ < δ₂} = (fun y => x + ι y + u y) '' (ball 0 δ₁ ∩ (fun y => x + ι y + u y) ⁻¹' S)) ∧ ∀ S : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet S → MeasurableSet (ball 0 δ₁ ∩ (fun y => x + ι y + u y) ⁻¹' S)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1–5 and 7 ((F1), (F3), (1a)) of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula (Simon 7.5.2 graph chart), with the chart data as hypotheses. Part (vi) is proved directly from the identity D ∩ G^{-1}(K) = π(K) ∩ G^{-1}(K), so it needs neither the graph property nor the relative closedness of N ∩ Z (parent steps 4–5). The conclusion, compactness of D ∩ G^{-1}(K), is the same as in parent step 5.

Notation. ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product. A := ι* is the adjoint, characterized by ⟨Aw, b⟩ = ⟨w, ιb⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left). π(w) := A(w − x).

1. (Linear algebra of ι.)
(a) Aι = id: ⟨Aιa, b⟩ = ⟨ιa, ιb⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩ for all b (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), so Aιa = a.
(b) If h ⊥ range ι then Ah = 0: ⟨Ah, b⟩ = ⟨h, ιb⟩ = 0 for all b.
(c) For every w ∈ ℝ^P, the vector w − x − ιπ(w) is ⊥ range ι. Indeed ⟨ιb, w − x − ιπ(w)⟩ = ⟨ιb, w − x⟩ − ⟨ιb, ιA(w − x)⟩ = ⟨ιb, w − x⟩ − ⟨b, A(w − x)⟩, and ⟨b, A(w − x)⟩ = ⟨A(w − x), b⟩ = ⟨w − x, ιb⟩, so the difference is 0.

2. (π∘G = id on D.) For v ∈ D, G(v) − x = ιv + u(v) and u(v) ⊥ range ι. So π(G(v)) = Aιv + Au(v) = v + 0 = v by 1(a) and 1(b).

3. (i) G = (constant x) + ι + u. Here ι is continuous linear (C^∞) and u is C² on D, so G is C² on D. In particular G is continuous on D, and u is differentiable at every v ∈ D (D is open and 2 ≥ 1).

4. (ii) For v ∈ D the sum rule gives DG(v) = 0 + ι + Du(v), i.e. DG(v)a = ιa + Du(v)a for every a.

5. (Du(v) maps into (range ι)^⊥.) Let v ∈ D and w ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, and put f(y) := ⟨ιw, u(y)⟩.
- f vanishes on the open set D ∋ v, so f agrees with the constant 0 near v and has derivative 0 at v.
- By the chain rule (⟨ιw, ·⟩ is continuous linear), f has derivative a ↦ ⟨ιw, Du(v)a⟩ at v.
- By uniqueness of the derivative, ⟨ιw, Du(v)a⟩ = 0 for all w, a ∈ ℝ^{n+1}.

6. (iii) Let v ∈ D and suppose DG(v)a = 0. By (ii), ιa + Du(v)a = 0. Take the inner product with ιa and use step 5: 0 = ⟨ιa, ιa⟩ + ⟨ιa, Du(v)a⟩ = |a|² + 0, so a = 0. DG(v) is linear with trivial kernel, hence injective.

7. (iv) If v, v' ∈ D and G(v) = G(v'), then v = π(G(v)) = π(G(v')) = v' by step 2.

8. (v) The maps w ↦ |π(w)| and w ↦ |w − x − ιπ(w)| are continuous. So Z = {w : |π(w)| < δ₁} ∩ {w : |w − x − ιπ(w)| < δ₂} is an intersection of two open sets, hence open (isOpen_lt, IsOpen.and).

9. (vi) Let K ⊆ Z be compact and K' := π(K).
- K' is compact (continuous image of a compact set).
- K' ⊆ D, because |π(w)| < δ₁ for every w ∈ Z.
- Claim: D ∩ G^{-1}(K) = K' ∩ G^{-1}(K). If v ∈ D and G(v) ∈ K, then v = π(G(v)) ∈ K' by step 2. Conversely, K' ⊆ D.
- G is continuous on K' ⊆ D, K' is closed (compact in a Hausdorff space) and K is closed. So K' ∩ G^{-1}(K) is closed (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed).
- As a closed subset of the compact set K', it is compact.

10. (vii) Let S ⊆ N.
(⊇) Let v ∈ D with G(v) ∈ S. Then G(v) ∈ Z:
- π(G(v)) = v (step 2) and |v| < δ₁.
- G(v) − x − ιπ(G(v)) = ιv + u(v) − ιv = u(v), and |u(v)| < δ₂/2 ≤ δ₂ (0 ≤ |u(v)| < δ₂/2 forces δ₂ > 0, hence δ₂/2 < δ₂).
Thus G(v) ∈ S ∩ Z.
(⊆) Let w ∈ S ∩ Z, v := π(w) and h := w − x − ιv.
- |v| < δ₁ and |h| < δ₂, because w ∈ Z.
- h ⊥ range ι by 1(c).
- x + ιv + h = w ∈ S ⊆ N.
The graph hypothesis gives h = u(v), so G(v) = x + ιv + u(v) = x + ιv + h = w. Since |v| < δ₁ we have v ∈ D, and G(v) = w ∈ S, so w ∈ G(D ∩ G^{-1}(S)).

11. (viii) Let G̃ := G on D and G̃ := x (constant) off D.
- G is continuous on the open, hence Borel, set D, and the constant is continuous on the complement. So G̃ is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise).
- G̃ = G on D, so D ∩ G^{-1}(S) = D ∩ G̃^{-1}(S).
- For Borel S this is the intersection of two Borel sets, hence Borel. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι*ι = id, ι* kills (range ι)^⊥, and w − x − ιι*(w − x) ⊥ range ι; with u ⊥ range ι this gives π∘G = id on D, so G is injective on D.
G is C² on D with DG(v) = ι + Du(v). Differentiating ⟨ιw, u⟩ ≡ 0 on the open set D gives Du(v) ⊥ range ι, so |DG(v)a| ≥ |a| and DG(v) is injective.
For compact K ⊆ Z, D ∩ G⁻¹(K) = π(K) ∩ G⁻¹(K) is a closed subset of the compact set π(K) ⊆ D, hence compact.
Graph uniqueness gives S ∩ Z = G(D ∩ G⁻¹(S)) for S ⊆ N. Z is open, and D ∩ G⁻¹(S) is Borel via the piecewise extension of G.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree on every hypothesis and all eight conclusions. Adjoint identities, differentiation of normality and the sum rule establish injectivity and the derivative formula. The compactness argument using π(K) is valid without assuming K ⊆ N or global continuity of G. Graph uniqueness and the measurable piecewise extension prove the remaining assertions. Radius positivity is derived wherever needed from the pointwise norm bound; empty-domain cases cause no gap.

subproblem.title: The zero extension of the vector field of a pulled-back n-form is C¹ with compact support in D
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open, let G : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be C² on D, and let ω : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P) be a C^∞ differential n-form (values: continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P). Assume C := D ∩ G^{-1}(tsupport ω) is compact.

Let e_0, …, e_n be the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}, DG(v) the derivative of G at v, and j.succAbove the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j}. Define Φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} by Φ(v) := Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j ω(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})·e_j for v ∈ D, and Φ(v) := 0 for v ∉ D.

Then Φ is C¹ on ℝ^{n+1}, Φ has compact support, and tsupport Φ ⊆ D.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (G : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (Φ : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)), IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 G D → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ω → IsCompact (D ∩ G ⁻¹' tsupport ω) → Φ = D.indicator (fun v => ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (j : ℕ) * ω (G v) (fun k => fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single (j.succAbove k) 1))) • EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ ∧ HasCompactSupport Φ ∧ tsupport Φ ⊆ D
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 6 of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula, stated for an arbitrary open set D and a map G that is C² on D. The parent proves in its step 5 that C = D ∩ G^{-1}(tsupport ω) is compact; here that is a hypothesis.

Notation. K := tsupport ω (a closed set); C := D ∩ G^{-1}(K); e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For y ∈ ℝ^{n+1} put c_j(y) := (−1)^j ω(G(y))(DG(y)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(y)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}) and Ψ(y) := Σ_j c_j(y)e_j, so that Φ = 1_D·Ψ.

1. (Ψ is C¹ on D.)
(a) ω is C^∞, in particular C², and G is C² on D, so y ↦ ω(G(y)) is C² on D (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn). Composing with the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMapCLM, the map y ↦ ω(G(y)), viewed as a continuous multilinear map, is C² on D, hence C¹ on D.
(b) G is C² on the open set D, so y ↦ DG(y) is C¹ on D (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, since 1 + 1 ≤ 2). Hence for every fixed vector a, y ↦ DG(y)a is C¹ on D (ContDiffOn.clm_apply with a constant), and so is y ↦ (DG(y)e_{j.succAbove k})_{k<n} ∈ (ℝ^P)^n (contDiffOn_pi).
(c) The evaluation map ev(α, b) := α(b_0, …, b_{n−1}), from (continuous n-linear forms on ℝ^P) × (ℝ^P)^n to ℝ, is C^∞, because it is the restriction of a continuous multilinear map to the diagonal. Concretely, in Mathlib:
- for B := ContinuousLinearMap.id on continuous multilinear forms, B.continuousMultilinearMapOption is a continuous multilinear map on the constant family indexed by Option (Fin n);
- it satisfies B.continuousMultilinearMapOption (fun _ ↦ (α, b)) = α b (continuousMultilinearMapOption_apply_eq_self, true by rfl);
- continuous multilinear maps are C^∞ (ContinuousMultilinearMap.contDiff);
- the diagonal p ↦ (fun _ ↦ p) is continuous linear, hence C^∞ (contDiff_pi of contDiff_id).
Composing the last two gives that ev is C^∞.
(d) Hence c_j(y) = (−1)^j ev(ω(G(y)), (DG(y)e_{j.succAbove k})_{k<n}) is C¹ on D: a C^∞ map composed with a map that is C¹ on D (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn, ContDiffOn.prodMk), times a constant. Then Ψ = Σ_j c_j e_j is C¹ on D (finite sums of C¹ scalars times constant vectors).

2. (Φ vanishes off C.) Let v ∉ C.
- If v ∉ D, then Φ(v) = 0 by definition.
- If v ∈ D, then G(v) ∉ K, so ω(G(v)) = 0, since a function vanishes outside its topological support (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Then every c_j(v) = 0 and Φ(v) = Ψ(v) = 0.
Hence support Φ ⊆ C.

3. (C is closed.) C is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^{n+1}, hence closed. So V := ℝ^{n+1} ∖ C is open, Φ ≡ 0 on V by step 2, and in particular Φ is C¹ on V.

4. (Φ is C¹ on D.) On D, Φ = Ψ, so Φ is C¹ on D by step 1 (ContDiffOn.congr).

5. (Φ is C¹ on ℝ^{n+1}.) Since C ⊆ D, the open sets D and V cover ℝ^{n+1}. Φ is C¹ on each of them, and C¹ is a local property on open sets, so Φ is C¹ on ℝ^{n+1} (Mathlib contDiff_of_contDiffOn_union_of_isOpen).

6. (Support.) C is closed and contains support Φ (step 2), so tsupport Φ = closure(support Φ) ⊆ C ⊆ D (closure_minimal). tsupport Φ is closed and contained in the compact set C, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); that is, Φ has compact support. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each coefficient c_j = (−1)^j ev(ω∘G, (DG e_{j.succAbove k})_k) is C¹ on D: ev is C^∞ (a continuous multilinear map restricted to the diagonal), ω∘G is C² on D and DG is C¹ on D.
Φ vanishes off C = D ∩ G⁻¹(tsupport ω), which is compact and hence closed.
The open sets D and ℝ^{n+1} ∖ C cover ℝ^{n+1}, and Φ is C¹ on each (Φ = Ψ on D, Φ = 0 off C), so Φ is C¹.
tsupport Φ ⊆ C ⊆ D, so Φ has compact support.

subproblem.title: Divergence of the vector field of a pulled-back n-form: trace DΦ(v) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n) on D
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open, let G : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be C² on D, and let ω : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P) be a C^∞ differential n-form (values: continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P).

Let e_0, …, e_n be the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}, DG(v) the derivative of G at v, and j.succAbove the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j}. Define Φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} by Φ(v) := Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j ω(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})·e_j for v ∈ D, and Φ(v) := 0 for v ∉ D.

Then for every v ∈ D, trace DΦ(v) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n), where d is the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (G : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (Φ : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)), IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 G D → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ω → Φ = D.indicator (fun v => ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (j : ℕ) * ω (G v) (fun k => fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single (j.succAbove k) 1))) • EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) → ∀ v ∈ D, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (n + 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ v : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1)) = exteriorDerivative ω (G v) (fun i => fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 11–12 of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula: (1d) pull-back commutes with d, and (1e) d becomes divergence (Simon 7.5.2 with Ch. 6, 2.34–2.35). The statement is for an arbitrary open set D and a map G that is C² on D. Of the C^∞ hypothesis on ω, only differentiability at the points G(v) is used.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For every y ∈ ℝ^{n+1} put:
- β(y) := ω(G(y))∘DG(y), the n-covector β(y)(b_0, …, b_{n−1}) = ω(G(y))(DG(y)b_0, …, DG(y)b_{n−1}) (Mathlib: (ω (G y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G y));
- ê^j := Fin.removeNth j e = (e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)});
- c_j(y) := (−1)^j ω(G(y))(DG(y)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(y)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)});
- Ψ(y) := Σ_j c_j(y)e_j.
Thus Φ = 1_D·Ψ.

1. (Localize.) Fix v ∈ D. D is open, so it is a neighbourhood of v, and Φ = Ψ on D. Hence Φ and Ψ agree on a neighbourhood of v, and DΦ(v) = DΨ(v) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).

2. (Coefficients through β.) For all y and j, β(y)(ê^j) = ω(G(y))(DG(y)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(y)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}), by ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply and (Fin.removeNth j e)(k) = e_{j.succAbove k}. Therefore c_j(y) = (−1)^j β(y)(ê^j).

3. (Differentiability at v.)
- G is C² on the open set D ∋ v, hence C² at v (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). So G is differentiable at v, and DG = fderiv ℝ G is C¹ at v (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right, since 1 + 1 ≤ 2), hence differentiable at v.
- ω is C^∞, hence differentiable at G(v), so y ↦ ω(G(y)) is differentiable at v (chain rule).
- The pull-back (α, L) ↦ α∘L is differentiable jointly in both arguments, so β is differentiable at v (Mathlib DifferentiableAt.continuousAlternatingMapCompContinuousLinearMap).
- Evaluating a covector at the fixed tuple ê^j is continuous linear in the covector, so y ↦ β(y)(ê^j) is differentiable at v.
- By step 2, c_j is differentiable at v with Dc_j(v) = (−1)^j D[y ↦ β(y)(ê^j)](v).

4. (Derivative of Ψ.) Ψ = Σ_j c_j e_j is a finite sum of differentiable scalars times constant vectors. So Ψ is differentiable at v with DΨ(v)a = Σ_j (Dc_j(v)a)e_j for all a ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. In particular the i-th coordinate of DΨ(v)e_i is Dc_i(v)e_i.

5. (Trace.) For a linear endomorphism L of ℝ^{n+1}, trace L = Σ_i (Le_i)_i, the trace of the matrix of L in the standard basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with the standard basis, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply). By steps 1, 4 and 3:
trace DΦ(v) = trace DΨ(v) = Σ_i Dc_i(v)e_i = Σ_i (−1)^i D[y ↦ β(y)(ê^i)](v)e_i.

6. (d of β in coordinates.) β is differentiable at v (step 3), so Mathlib extDeriv_apply gives dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[y ↦ β(y)(Fin.removeNth i e)](v)(e_i). Here the integer (−1)^i acts on reals as multiplication by the real number (−1)^i. Comparing with step 5: trace DΦ(v) = dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n).

7. (Pull-back commutes with d.) Apply Mathlib extDeriv_pullback with ω differentiable at G(v), G C² at v, and minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2 (minSmoothness_of_isRCLikeNormedField). It gives dβ(v) = dω(G(v))∘DG(v) as (n+1)-covectors, where β is exactly the map x ↦ (ω (G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x) of that lemma. Evaluating at (e_0, …, e_n): dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n).

8. (Conclusion.) Steps 6 and 7 give trace DΦ(v) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n) for every v ∈ D. ∎
proof_key_steps: Near v ∈ D (D open), Φ equals Ψ = Σ_j c_j e_j, so trace DΦ(v) = Σ_i Dc_i(v)e_i.
c_j(y) = (−1)^j β(y)(removeNth j e) for the pulled-back form β(y) = ω(G(y))∘DG(y), which is differentiable at v because G is C² at v.
extDeriv_apply: dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[β(·)(removeNth i e)](v)e_i, which equals trace DΦ(v).
extDeriv_pullback (G C² at v): dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n).

audit.reason: The prose and frozen type match exactly. Openness permits replacing Φ locally by Ψ before differentiating. Differentiability of the pullback and coefficients justifies the trace computation; extDeriv_apply supplies the correct signs and succAbove ordering. The stated C² hypothesis satisfies extDeriv_pullback, completing the identity without compact-support assumptions or reliance on another child.

subproblem.title: Injective-immersion area formula on a Borel subset of ℝ^m with Gram-determinant Jacobian
subproblem.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, and let F ⊆ ℝ^m be a Borel set. Assume G is differentiable at every v ∈ F with injective derivative DG(v), and G is injective on F. Let e_0, …, e_{m−1} be the standard basis of ℝ^m.

Then for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ:
∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j<m})^{1/2} · h(G(v)) dL^m(v).

Here H^m = μHE[m] is the normalized m-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m. Both sides are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed, and a non-integrable integral is 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P) (F : Set (Euclid m)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ v ∈ F, DifferentiableAt ℝ G v) → (∀ v ∈ F, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G v)) → InjOn G F → ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ w in G '' F, h w ∂μHE[m] = ∫ v in F, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))) * h (G v)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 9 ((1b), area formula) of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula, stated for an arbitrary dimension m, map G and Borel set F (Simon Ch. 2, (3.3)–(3.5)).

Implementation note: the proof uses SimonGMT's Chapter02 area formula, so GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean must add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`. There is precedent: accepted solution commit c2cf4bd9 added `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz`. The statement itself only uses notions already imported.

1. (SimonGMT area formula.) Apply SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean) with:
- source space E = ℝ^m and target ℝ^P;
- s = F (measurable);
- f = G, which is differentiable at every point of F with injective derivative and injective on F;
- integrand h.
It gives ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[finrank ℝ^m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v • h(G(v)) dμHE[finrank ℝ^m](v). This identity holds for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ without integrability hypotheses. It is derived from the measure identity map(G|_F)(J·μHE⌞F) = μHE⌞G(F) via MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀.

2. (Normalize the measures.) finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). On ℝ^m, μHE[finrank ℝ^m] equals Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G(v)) dv.

3. (Gram form of the Jacobian.) Fix v ∈ F and put L := DG(v).
- By definition areaJacobianAt G v = normDet(L) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), and normDet(L) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg).
- Apply Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram to the linear map L and the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun of ℝ^m, whose vectors are e_i. It gives normDet(L)² = det Gram(Le_0, …, Le_{m−1}), where Matrix.gram ℝ w i j = ⟨w_i, w_j⟩; that is, normDet(L)² = det[⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩]_{i,j}.
- Taking the nonnegative square root (Real.sqrt_sq): areaJacobianAt G v = (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j})^{1/2}.
(Equivalently: normDet(L)² = det(L*L), and the matrix of L*L in the orthonormal basis (e_i) has entries ⟨e_i, L*Le_j⟩ = ⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩.)

4. (Conclusion.) Substitute step 3 into the right side of step 2 pointwise on the measurable set F (setIntegral_congr_fun; the scalar action is real multiplication). This gives ∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2} h(G(v)) dv. ∎
proof_key_steps: SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative: ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G v) dμHE for every h, with no integrability hypothesis.
On ℝ^m, finrank = m and μHE[m] = volume.
areaJacobianAt G v = normDet DG(v) = (det Gram(DG(v)e_i))^{1/2}, by normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the standard orthonormal basis and normDet ≥ 0; then setIntegral_congr_fun on F.
